question.text: A commodity's spot price is Rs 5,000. Interest rate is 12% p.a. compounded continuously. What is the 3-month futures fair value? (e^0.03 = 1.03045)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pp.53-54, F = S x e^(r x n). Here F = 5,000 x e^(0.12 x 3/12) = 5,000 x e^0.03 = 5,000 x 1.03045 = Rs 5,152.25. The Trap: Rs 5,150 uses simple interest. Rs 5,600 uses the full year instead of 3/12. Rs 5,030.45 forgets to multiply by 5,000. Note: Use the given e^0.03 value directly and convert the time horizon to years (3/12) before computing the exponent.
